subject: Performance tiering MAP & evaluation kickoff
messages:
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
To: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@acmecloud.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 18 Jan 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Performance tiering MAP & evaluation kickoff

Sanjay —

Thanks again for the time earlier. Per our call, I’m kicking off a mutual action plan (MAP) focused on the performance benchmarking that we agreed would drive your HW-buy decision. Attached is an initial spreadsheet with the proposed evaluation matrix and timelines (performance-tiering-map-v1.xlsx).

High-level goals (please confirm):
- Latency: 95th pct latency for customer-facing generation routes <= 250ms (TTFT target < 180ms)
- Throughput: sustained throughput targets for batch embedding routes >= 2000 tokens/s
- Concurrency: validate stability at target concurrency bands (1, 8, 32, 128)
- Isolation: explore MIG configs for multi-tenant safety and quota enforcement

Proposed next steps:
1) You share workload traces / sample prompts (anonymized) — we’ll use these to pick sequence length dist.
2) Redwood runs a 2-week eval across A100 (full), H100 (full), and L40S (full + MIG splits).
3) Deliver: consolidated performance report, cost-per-token estimates, and recommended fleet mix.

Timeline suggestion: decision checkpoint by 2026-02-05, pilot on chosen fleet in March.

Please confirm the goals and share traces; I’ve cc’d Monica & Rishi to own the test matrix and runbook.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
attachments: performance-tiering-map-v1.xlsx

From: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@acmecloud.com>

Date: Mon, 19 Jan 2026 11:03:12 -0800
Subject: Re: Performance tiering MAP & evaluation kickoff

Kimberly —

Thanks, this looks good. I confirmed the high-level goals internally. Two quick things from our side:
- I’ve attached a set of anonymized workload traces and a small sample prompt set (acme-traces-20260119.tar.gz). They skew short (avg prompt ~ 40 tokens) but we have a tail of long instructions (~1k tokens) for admin-reporting flows.
- I’m looping in Bjorn from EdgeCompute; they’ve run similar MIG experiments and can share lessons learned.

On isolation: we’re leaning to MIG for multi-tenant staging but want to understand the TTFT hit for small-generation workloads. If MIG adds ~30% TTFT, that might be acceptable for batch/embeds but not for our customer-facing flows.

We’re available for the pilot week of Jan 26 — can Redwood schedule initial runs then?

Sanjay Rao
Head of Platform Engineering, Acme Cloud Solutions
attachments: acme-traces-20260119.tar.gz

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 20 Jan 2026 08:27:45 -0800
Subject: Re: Performance tiering MAP & evaluation kickoff

Kim / Rishi —

Draft test matrix and runbook (high level):
- Hardware variants: A100-40GB (full), H100-80GB (full), L40S-48GB (full), L40S MIG splits (2-way / 4-way).
- Models to test: generation medium (seq model v2.1 16k), instruction-tuned chat model (8k), embeddings model (dense-encoder).
- Metrics: TTFT (time-to-first-token), per-token latency, 50/95/99 latency percentiles, aggregate tokens/sec, GPU memory footprint, kernel saturation (SM utilization), and tail latency under KV-cache warm start vs cold start.
- Concurrency bands: single-client low-latency (1), moderate (8), high (32), stress (128).
- Prompt length distribution: 70% short (<64), 25% mid (64-512), 5% long (>512) — will use Acme traces to validate.

MIG-specific notes:
- Test MIG 1:1, 1:2, 1:4 splits where applicable; capture TTFT impact per split.
- Evaluate KV cache warm-up impacts by running repeat requests and measuring first vs steady tokens/sec.

Run cadence:
- Jan 26–28: baseline runs (cold + warm cache) across all hardware types at concurrency 1/8/32.
- Feb 1–4: denser stress runs including 128 concurrency and long prompt tails.
- Feb 5: delivery of consolidated numbers and recommended fleet mix for decision checkpoint.

I’ve sketched this out in a doc (mig-vs-full-gpu-plan.md). Rishi — can you wire up the run scripts and make sure we capture kernel-level metrics?

—Monica
Principal Performance Engineer, Redwood Inference
attachments: mig-vs-full-gpu-plan.md

From: Bjorn Andersson <bjorn@edgecompute.io>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>, Sanjay Rao <sanjay@acmecloud.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 21 Jan 2026 14:40:22 +0100
Subject: Re: Performance tiering MAP & evaluation kickoff

Kim / team —

Quick note from our prior MIG experiments (attached a short extract: edge-mini-results.csv):
- L40S 4-way MIG gives excellent packing (3.8x density vs full GPU) but TTFT increased by ~28–35% on our short prompt workload.
- H100 full beat A100 on steady tokens/sec for long-sequence runs (>= 1k tokens) by ~18%, and kernel utilization was much higher (fewer stalls).
- MIG 2-way was a reasonable compromise: much of the TTFT overhead is in setup/SM context switching — 2-way kept TTFT within ~12% of full GPU for many gen models.

A few suggestions for your runbook:
- Include a KV-cache warm-up step (send 10 warm requests before measuring steady state).
- Capture cold-start TTFT separately — it’s often the driver for perceived latency in user-facing flows.
- Record p95/p99 both with and without cache.

Happy to share more logs from our runs if helpful.

Best,
Bjorn Andersson
Performance Lead, EdgeCompute (vendor)
attachments: edge-mini-results.csv

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
To: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@acmecloud.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Bjorn Andersson <bjorn@edgecompute.io>
Date: Thu, 22 Jan 2026 16:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Performance tiering MAP & evaluation kickoff — consolidated plan & next steps

Sanjay —

Thanks for the traces and Bjorn for the early notes. We ran an initial sweep this week and attached a short summary with topline recommendations (performance-tiering-summary-20260122.pdf). Key takeaways: 

Topline recommendations (for discussion at the 2026-02-05 checkpoint):
- H100 (full) as the primary platform for low-latency, customer-facing generation routes — best p95/p99 for long sequences and steady throughput.
- L40S MIG (2-way preferred) for mixed workloads where higher density matters — acceptable TTFT tradeoff for embeds and batch generation when KV-cache warm-up is feasible.
- A100 as a fallback/spot capacity for cost-sensitive background workloads; performance gap vs H100 is small for shorter sequences.

Operational notes:
- We observed a 20–35% TTFT delta between full GPU and 4-way MIG on short prompts; 2-way MIG reduced that delta substantially.
- KV-cache warm start reduces steady-token-perf variance dramatically — include warm-up in SLAs for low-latency routes.

Deliverables & timeline:
- Jan 26–Feb 4: full MAP runs (per Monica’s runbook).
- Feb 5: checkpoint meeting to review consolidated numbers and pick preferred fleet mix.
- Mar 01–31: pilot of chosen fleet in Acme staging (hardware & costs to be finalized with procurement).

Action items for Acme: share any constraints on procurement (preferred vendors, spot vs reserved), confirm decision approver list, and sign off on the KPI targets above.

I’ll also open a PR to add the run scripts and dashboards — Rishi, Monica please confirm you’ve got the instrumentation hooks.

Thanks all — looking forward to the pilot.

—Kimberly Park
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
